scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation” (preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 145 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 45000cec6bcec95d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation is mixing of every finite order. More explicitly, under the assumptions above, for every k ≥ 3 and every A1, . . . , Ak ∈ F, µ A1 ∩ T−n1 A2 ∩ · · · ∩ T−(n1+···+nk−1) Ak  −→ k Y i=1 µ(Ai) as min(n1, . . . , nk−1) → ∞ through positive integers. No standardness or countable-generation assumption is imposed on the original probability space.
